params.body:
Each request in a forwarded mail now becomes a GitHub issue, and the pull request that solves it closes it. The repository's history then shows why a change was made, not only what changed.

The task `mail-intake.mjs` gives a session says:
- **One issue per request,** not one per mail: a mail with two requests gets two issues. It is opened with `hand.mjs issue --labels mail` in the repository the request concerns, before anything is built.
- **The body** is the request in the session's own words, why it matters, and `Portal mail:<id>` as the source. **No personal data** of the sender or of anyone the mail mentions: names, addresses and phone numbers stay in Portal.
- **A request that is already an open issue** gets no second one. Reading issues needs control#95 (`issues: read` on the read token); until that is rolled out, the session cannot see existing issues.
- **Each pull request says `Closes #<n>`.** The mail goes to done with the issue numbers in its note.

The README section on forwarded mail says the same. `node --check` passes.
params.title: Forwarded mail: each request an issue, each pull request closes one
